title: Automated efficiency loss analysis by luminescence image reconstruction using generative adversarial networks
mechanism: A GAN reconstructs a defect-free luminescence image of a cell; the difference to the real image isolates defects and quantifies their efficiency loss.
adaptation: Train a masked inpainting U-Net on the 11.9k unlabelled pool cells; feed abs(EL - reconstruction) as a second input channel to the house model, as an anomaly prior that does not depend on the learned full-cell layout (target: E1, where 70% of crack pixels get p(crack) < 0.001). Scuffs will also light up, so watch precision.
min_experiment: Arm: house with 2-channel input (EL, residual); baseline: house. Metrics: E1 crack recall and relF1@2, CV crack relF1@2 as guard. Kill if E1 recall < +0.03 or CV relF1@2 drops > 0.01.
evidence: R: reconstruction-based loss analysis on luminescence images of silicon cells (companion PVSC 2021 doi:10.1109/pvsc43889.2021.9518512); numbers not retrieved.
prior_overlap: none. MIM / DDeP pretraining (n.d.) used reconstruction for features only; residual-as-input and anomaly priors are on the never-tried list.
